segments.text: We show that a very small neural network can learn a toy task in a handful of epochs. We describe the model, the loss we minimise, and a comparison against two baselines.

segments.text: L of theta equals minus one over N, times the sum over i of y sub i, times the log of y hat sub i.

segments.text: Let's unpack that. Theta is everything the model can learn, its weights. For each training example, y is the true answer and y hat is the probability the model gave it. Taking the log of that probability and flipping the sign means the loss is small when the model is confident and right, and grows sharply when it's confidently wrong. Dividing by N just averages this over all the examples. So minimising L simply means: push the model to put high probability on the correct answers.
